subject: Regional partner localization & data residency: APAC/EU SI playbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Keiko Tanaka <keiko@sakai-systems.jp>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Regional partner localization & data residency: APAC/EU SI playbook

Hi Keiko,

Great meeting last week — thanks for walking through Sakai's enterprise pipeline in Japan and APAC. Per our conversation, Sakai is interested in a quick pilot (POC) where Redwood runs inference in a VPC with region-specific controls, and Sakai helps with systems integration and customer introductions. Two topics came up that we should capture in a short playbook:

- Data residency / on-prem vs managed VPC requirements per customer
- Consent and logging workflow (what we surface to SI for audits)
- Commercial model for regional SIs (referral vs reseller vs co-sell)

Can you confirm if Sakai can: (1) accept a brief SOW for a 6-week POC, (2) provide an initial list of target customers with residency constraints, and (3) share a local proof-of-concept timeline? I attached a one-page SOW template and a proposed SI localization checklist to make it easy.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm POC SOW acceptance (this week)
- Redwood provides an APAC/EU playbook draft by Jan 27
- Quick sync to align on audit artifacts (SOC2 extracts, access logs)

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if useful.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SI_Localization_Checklist.xlsx, Sakai_POC_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Keiko Tanaka <keiko@sakai-systems.jp>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-22T10:34:00+09:00
Subject: Re: Regional partner localization & data residency: APAC/EU SI playbook

Hi Karthik,

Thanks — Sakai is excited to move forward. Quick answers:

1) We can sign the 6-week POC SOW; legal will review minor local clauses.
2) Initial customers: two banks (Tokyo, Osaka) and an e-commerce retailer with explicit Japan-only data residency. I can share redacted briefs by EOD Monday.
3) Timeline: target start Feb 8, demo to customers in week 6.

On logging/audit artifacts: we need to see retention windows and whether audit logs include request-level metadata (IP, model version, token counts). If Redwood can provide a template audit pack, we will map against local compliance.

I'll loop in our legal lead if any contract redlines happen.

—
Keiko Tanaka
Head of Systems Integration, Sakai Systems
keiko@sakai-systems.jp
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-23T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Regional partner localization & data residency: APAC/EU SI playbook

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick internal notes after Keiko's reply:

- Legal: Redwood can provide a SOC2 extract and sanitized access logs; retention windows are configurable per customer but default 30 days for request traces. Need DataTrust to confirm EU data transfer controls.
- Product: For POC, we'll propose a managed VPC in ap-northeast-1 with optional on-prem connector for customers that insist. Sequence: provisioning -> model pinning -> sample audit pack.
- GTM: recommend a 50/30/20 split for referral/reseller/co-sell economics for the pilot cohort. Keep pricing transparent in SOW.

I'll draft the playbook skeleton and share a Google Drive folder with checklist and SOW template by Friday.

LB
Lauren Bishop
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
From: contracts@datatrust.de <contracts@datatrust.de>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oliver Bates <oliver.bates@dataprivacy.co.uk>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-28T08:21:00+01:00
Subject: Data residency Q/A and transfer controls for EU customers

Karthik / team,

Following up from our intro call, please find attached a short Q/A doc with the specific transfer controls we typically need for EU customers that will be named in the SOW. High-level:

- We require documented processing locations and subprocessors for the entire inference pipeline.
- If any telemetry crosses outside the EU, we need SCCs in place or adequacy via a specific cloud region.
- Access logs must retain request metadata for 90 days for our customers in regulated sectors.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you provide a list of subprocessors (managed infra vendors) and their regions?
2) Is there a hardened logging mode with 90-day retention and exportable CSVs?
3) For APAC customers with strict residency, can you run a fully private deployment (VPC control plane) in ap-southeast-1 under customer-managed keys?

We attached DataResidency_QA_responses.docx for reference. Please reply with a point-by-point answer so legal can sign off.

Best,
DataTrust GmbH (legal ops)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Keiko Tanaka <keiko@sakai-systems.jp>, contracts@datatrust.de
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-02T16:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Regional partner localization & data residency: APAC/EU SI playbook

Keiko / DataTrust team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answers inline and next steps below.

1) Subprocessors: AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1), GCP for specific marketplace customers (eu-west-1), and a single CDN provider (FastEdge) for non-sensitive static assets. Full subprocessors list and regions in Drive (link below).

2) Logging: We have a hardened logging profile that retains request-level metadata for up to 90 days and can export CSVs on-demand. For the POC we'll enable the hardened profile and provide export samples.

3) Private deployment: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC with KMS integration. For APAC customers that require fully private air-gapped options, we can scope an on-prem package but that will affect timeline and cost.

Action items:
- Karthik: share draft playbook and SOW in Drive (done) -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSI-playbook
- Keiko: share redacted customer briefs by Jan 26 (received)
- DataTrust: confirm SCC vs adequacy requirement for the named customers; Marissa to coordinate legal artifacts transfer
- Lauren: finalize partner economics and POC pricing; attach in SOW v1

I'll prepare a one-page summary for Sakai's customers and a checklist for legal artifacts. Attaching the consolidated QA doc.

Thanks — will schedule a follow-up on Feb 5 to finalize SOW.

Karthik
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DataResidency_QA_responses.docx, SI_Localization_Checklist.xlsx
